summary: rollup-plugin-polyfill-helper executes remote code fetched from rest-icon-helper.store
details: The package presents itself as a rollup polyfill helper but its exported functions (getPlugin, setPlugin, getPluginExten) issue HTTPS requests to a hardcoded host rest-icon-helper.store at paths /icons/303 and /icons/389 and pass the response body through eval(JSON.parse(b)), giving the operator of that host arbitrary code execution inside the consumer's Node.js process whenever the advertised API is invoked. The destination URL is assembled at runtime from separate protocol/separator/subdomain/domain/path fragments, function names are chosen to resemble legitimate rollup plugin helpers, and a platform check delays the second fetch-and-eval by 60 seconds on non-Windows hosts. The name, identifiers, and cover story do not match the observed behavior of fetching and evaluating remote code from a non-publisher domain.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
